stemBlocks.value: A merchant bought a radio for $4 500 and sold it for $5 400. (a) Calculate the profit. (b) Calculate the percentage profit.
Think first: Profit is a difference; percentage profit is that difference measured against the cost price.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p019-q16 from workbook page 19.

solutionSteps.instruction: Subtract the cost price from the selling price.
Divide the profit by the COST price.

strategyBlocks.value: Subtract cost price from selling price to get the profit, then express the profit as a percentage of the cost price.

whyThisWorks.value: Percentage profit measures how well the money tied up in the item performed, so the cost price is the base. Using the selling price instead would give 16.7%, which answers a different question about margin. Cost price as the denominator is the standard convention in profit and loss.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing the profit by the selling price instead of the cost price.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing the profit by the selling price instead of the cost price.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the selling price as the profit.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Giving the selling price as the profit.
Avoid this: Writing 0.2 as the final percentage.

examTip.value: Underline the cost price as soon as you read it. It is the denominator for both percentage profit and percentage loss.
